SharonAI.overview: First Nasdaq-listed (SHAZ) Australian neocloud with live GPU infrastructure in certified sovereign facilities. Operating H100, H200, B200 and Blackwell Ultra clusters at NEXTDC Melbourne and Sydney. Partnered with Cisco and NVIDIA to launch Australia's first Cisco Secure AI Factory. Targeting 20,000+ GPUs by end of 2026.

sovereignty.notes: All data processing remains in Australia. Cisco Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA supports Australia's National AI Plan.

networking.notes: Built on NVIDIA HGX reference architecture with BlueField-3 DPUs for secure sovereign networking.

kubernetes.notes: Lightweight scalable container environments for AI deployment. GPU-native orchestration on bare metal NEXTDC infrastructure.

inference.notes: Inference capability available via enterprise agreement. No public self-serve inference API as of May 2026. Primarily GPUaaS and enterprise contracts.

pricing.notes: No public per-GPU pricing. Enterprise and government contracts. Minimum commitments apply. Contact sales for AUD-denominated pricing.

pros: Only Nasdaq-listed sovereign Australian AI cloud
Live GPU fleet — H100, H200, B200, Blackwell Ultra operational now
NEXTDC Tier IV facilities — 100% uptime SLA
Cisco Secure AI Factory — first in Australia
Supports Australian National AI Plan
AUD billing available for Australian entities
BlueField-3 DPUs for secure sovereign networking
cons: No public self-serve pricing — enterprise only
No public managed inference API yet
Smaller GPU fleet than global providers (scaling in 2026)
Limited to Australian data centres currently
Higher cost premium for sovereignty
SharonAI.bestFor: Australian enterprises, government, and research organisations requiring sovereign AI compute with data remaining in Australia

Firmus.overview: NVIDIA-backed Australian neocloud at $5.5B valuation (April 2026). Recognised as Top 3 Global GPU Cloud by SemiAnalysis. Building 1.6GW AI factory capacity across Australia via Project Southgate. First AI Factory Zone established in Tasmania powered by hydro. DCD Asia-Pacific Data Centre Project of the Year 2024.

sovereignty.notes: Tasmanian hydro-powered AI Factory Zone is Australia's first sovereign AI infrastructure zone. Model-to-Grid architecture integrates energy and compute.

networking.directConnect: Via VAST Data AI OS unified fabric
networking.notes: Model-to-Grid architecture: AI Factory is grid-aware and model-aware simultaneously. Synert software platform integrates networking, thermal and grid signals.

kubernetes.service: AI Cloud — GPU clusters and on-demand instances
features: VAST Data AI OS storage layer
kubernetes.notes: Vertically integrated system — model behaviour, GPU performance, thermal dynamics and grid conditions unified into one optimisation framework.

inference.notes: Firmus is infrastructure-only at this stage. No managed inference API. Customers deploy their own inference stack on Firmus AI Factories.

pricing.notes: No public pricing. Hyperscale and enterprise contracts. GB300 cluster deployment. Pre-IPO — pricing expected to become more accessible post-ASX listing.

pros: NVIDIA-backed at $5.5B valuation — well capitalised
Top 3 Global GPU Cloud (SemiAnalysis 2024 & 2025)
Hydro-powered Tasmania facility — lowest carbon AI compute in Australia
18,500 GB300 GPUs at Southgate Melbourne (April 2026)
Vertically integrated Model-to-Grid architecture
VAST Data AI OS — unified storage, compute and networking
1.6GW planned capacity — largest Australian AI infrastructure build
cons: Pre-IPO — limited public transparency on pricing
Infrastructure-only — no managed inference product
Minimum cluster-level commitments
Most capacity still being built (2026-2027)
Not accessible for small teams or developers
Firmus.bestFor: Large enterprises, hyperscalers, and government requiring Australian sovereign AI training infrastructure at scale with clean energy

Micron21.tagline: Australia's first Tier IV GPU cloud
Micron21.overview: Melbourne-based neocloud operating Australia's first Tier IV-certified data centre (MEL1). Self-serve GPU cloud (mGPU) with A10, A100, RTX A6000, H100, and H200 on OpenStack. Offers dedicated GPU passthrough and time-sliced contended access. 100% uptime guarantee. 24/7 Australian-based support. Positions as significantly cheaper than AWS, Azure, and GCP for AU workloads.

sovereignty.notes: Australia's first and only Tier IV certified DC. 100% uptime SLA. All data remains in AU.

networking.bandwidth: High-speed NVMe SSD + enterprise networking fabric
networking.egress: Included in plans (no per-GB fees on most tiers)
networking.directConnect: Via Equinix and IX Australia peering
networking.notes: OpenStack-based platform with GPU passthrough. Intel Xeon Gold CPUs + NVMe SSDs. HA architecture standard.

kubernetes.notes: OpenShift available on mCloud platform with GPU integration. Self-serve via mCloud dashboard.

inference.type: GPUaaS only — no managed inference API
inference.notes: No managed inference product. Deploy your own vLLM, TGI, or TensorRT-LLM stack on mGPU instances. Self-serve via mCloud portal.

pricing.pricingModel: Transparent pricing via online calculator — AUD denominated
pricing.notes: Pricing via online calculator at micron21.com/calculator. AUD pricing. Positions as fraction of AWS/Azure/GCP cost. No per-GB egress fees on most plans.

pros: Only self-serve AU GPU cloud with Tier IV certification
A100, H100, H200 available today in Melbourne
AUD pricing — no currency risk for AU customers
No per-GB egress fees on standard plans
24/7 Australian-based support team
OpenShift + GPU integration for K8s workloads
Significantly cheaper than hyperscalers per their TCO analysis
cons: Pricing not publicly listed — requires calculator/quote
Single data centre (Melbourne only) — no multi-region
Smaller GPU fleet than hyperscalers or Sharon AI
No InfiniBand for multi-node training at scale
No managed inference product
Less known globally than major neoclouds
Micron21.bestFor: Australian SMEs and enterprises wanting self-serve GPU compute with AU data residency, Tier IV reliability, and AUD billing — without hyperscaler pricing

IREN.overview: NASDAQ-listed (IREN) AU-founded AI cloud provider with $9.7B Microsoft contract and 150,000 GPU target by end 2026. Headquarters in Sydney but GPU infrastructure in Texas (Childress) and British Columbia (Mackenzie, Prince George). Transitioning from Bitcoin mining to AI cloud. AU projects 'advancing' but no live AU GPU cloud yet as of May 2026.

sovereignty.notes: AU-founded company but all live GPU infrastructure is in US and Canada. AU data centre projects are in development — not yet operational as of May 2026.

networking.bandwidth: 200MW+ liquid-cooled data centres with NDR InfiniBand
networking.notes: Vertically integrated platform: owns land, power, data centres, and GPU stack. Horizon 1-4 liquid-cooled clusters at Childress targeting 200MW IT load.

kubernetes.notes: Acquired Mirantis in 2026 to strengthen K8s delivery. Primarily large-scale GPU clusters for Microsoft and hyperscale customers.

inference.notes: Primary customer is Microsoft ($9.7B contract). Also serves other hyperscale and enterprise customers. No public self-serve access.

pricing.notes: No public pricing. Revenue of $3.7B ARR targeted by end 2026 via Microsoft and other hyperscale contracts. Not accessible to SMEs.

pros: AU-founded — Sydney HQ, ASX/NASDAQ listed (IREN)
$9.7B Microsoft contract validates platform quality
150,000 GPU fleet (H100, H200, B300) by end 2026
Vertically integrated — owns power, land, DC, and GPUs
Mirantis acquisition strengthens K8s delivery
Renewable energy-powered infrastructure
cons: No GPU infrastructure in Australia — all US/Canada
Not AU sovereign for data residency purposes
Enterprise/hyperscale only — not accessible to AU SMEs
No public self-serve pricing or sign-up
Primarily a Microsoft infrastructure partner, not general cloud
AU projects still in development — no live AU capacity
IREN.bestFor: Context only — AU-founded company but not relevant for AU sovereign data requirements. Watch for AU expansion in 2027+

SCX.ai.tagline: Australia's first sovereign AI inference node
SCX.ai.overview: Sydney-based sovereign AI inference company using ASIC-based (non-GPU) inference chips. Launched Australia's first sovereign AI inference node in January 2026 at Equinix SY5 in Sydney. Claims 10x efficiency vs traditional GPU-based systems with zero water cooling. Focuses on enterprise and government AI inference with strict data sovereignty.

sovereignty.notes: Purpose-built for AU sovereign AI inference. ASIC chips eliminate water cooling — critical for AU data centre power/water constraints. Lowest carbon footprint per AI token claimed.

networking.bandwidth: Enterprise carrier-neutral connectivity at Equinix SY5
networking.directConnect: Via Equinix cross-connects to all major AU carriers
networking.notes: Equinix SY5 provides direct access to AU's internet exchange and enterprise carrier ecosystem.

kubernetes.notes: Not a general compute platform. Inference-only. No K8s or GPU training capability.

inference.notes: ASIC-based (not GPU). 10x efficiency vs GPU inference. No water cooling. Targeted at AU government and regulated enterprise needing sovereign inference. First live sovereign AU inference node.

pricing.notes: No public pricing. ASIC-based inference pricing model differs from GPU-hour billing. Contact for enterprise/government pricing.

pros: First sovereign AI inference node live in Australia (Jan 2026)
ASIC-based — 10x efficiency vs GPU inference
Zero water cooling — sustainable and AU climate-appropriate
Lowest carbon footprint per AI token claimed
Equinix SY5 — carrier-neutral, enterprise-grade connectivity
Purpose-built for AU government and regulated industries
cons: ASIC-only — no GPU training capability
Inference-only — not a general compute platform
No public pricing or self-serve access
Very early stage — limited track record
Not compatible with standard GPU workloads
No OpenAI-compatible API publicly available
SCX.ai.bestFor: Australian government and regulated enterprises needing sovereign AI inference with maximum efficiency and no water cooling dependency
